messages:
marta: kicking off Q2 periodic access review. goal: verify admin entitlements + owner evidence for all KMS-granted roles by next Fri (2024-05-03). please reply with owners or mark "no access needed" for any roles you control. attach evidence links if possible. :calendar:

jordan: thanks. do we have a defined scope? only production projects or staging too?

marta: scope = production + payment-related staging namespaces. non-prod infra (dev/test) excluded unless flagged as admin.

samir: noted. quick Q on KMS: do we treat cross-account grants as admin entitlements for this review?

marta: yes — any grant that yields write/Decrypt privileges counts. we want owner + justification.

lee: i ran a quick query against the audit index, found 3 service principals with admin grants and no owners. snippet:
```sql
SELECT principal, key_id, grant_type, last_used_at
FROM kms_grants
WHERE privilege IN ("Encrypt","Decrypt","CreateKey","ScheduleKeyDeletion")
  AND last_used_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '180 days'
  AND owner IS NULL;
```

lee: results pasted to the shared doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/access-q2-kms-snapshot (sheet tab: unowned-grants)

auditbot: automated check: 3 ownerless admin grants detected (lee's query). ticket created: SEC-3721.

ashley: For audit logs retention — are we expanding retention for this review to 400 days? that would help for slower owners. DB/storage cost impact?

devops: expansion to 400d is ok for the review window if we snapshot to cold storage; i'll run a one-off snapshot and upload link to the doc. btw make sure SQL above is rate-limited; heavy scans spike the cluster.

jordan: also flagging one user with temporary elevation (u/alex.t) — expiration was 2024-02-20 but grant still exists. who owns that service?

marta: good catch. alex.t elevation -> owner is payments-platform team. @samir can you confirm and remove if it's stale?

samir: checking now. found change request 3245 that requested the elevation for debugging — it was approved but the follow-up revoke task didn't complete. i'll revoke and post PR to the entitlement-scrub repo.

lee: small suggestion: add an automated canary that denies admin grants older than 90 days with no owner, but only blocks new grants. want to avoid breakage.

marta: that's a policy improvement. can we make it an advisory first and then enforce after 30 days?

devops: yes, we can implement advisory alerts in the entitlement-linter. rule payload example:
```yaml
rule: owner-required-or-expiring
conditions:
  - grant_age > 90d
  - owner == null
action: advisory_alert
notify: #security, #payments
```

ashley: also need to confirm audit logging for KMS key policy changes — set retention and alerting on policy drift events. we missed one in Jan.

marta: action items summary: 1) samir revoke alex.t stale elevation + PR link; 2) lee verify owners for 3 ownerless grants (document evidence); 3) devops snapshot logs to cold storage and enable advisory rule; 4) ashley configure policy-drift alerts and set retentions; 5) jordan coordinate payments staging review. owners assigned in doc. deadline: 2024-05-03 EOD.

samir: on it — will update SEC-3721 and attach revoke PR.

lee: i've added owner evidence for 2/3 grants; last one needs product signoff (cc: jordan).

jordan: product signoff given for that last grant; added comment in the sheet.

auditbot: SEC-3721 updated: status = in_progress, owners = [samir, lee, jordan], due = 2024-05-03.

marta: thanks everyone. small procedural note: when you mark "no access needed" please include the minimal justification (why the grant exists and who will re-request if needed). keeps the audit trail clean. :memo:

devops: FYI i'll create an infra runbook snippet for future sweeps and add a one-click owner assignment flow in the console.

marta: perfect. we'll reconvene after the deadline for a short post-check retro. closing thread for now — ping me if blockers. :v:
